clue.text: It guides a ploughman

definitions.meaning: the steering bar of a boat directs its course
a farm worker who tills the soil is one who tills

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what steers a farmer as he ploughs his field.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: the bar a helmsman steers with, and someone who tills the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a boat's steering lever and a person who cultivates ground.

clue.text: Refuse to fold over the sheet?

definitions.meaning: to reject or decline an offer
the folded-back top sheet of a made bed

explanation.surface: Declining to fold back the bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb it means decline; as a noun it is the folded-back bedding of a hotel bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline an offer, and the folding back of bedding ready for sleep.

clue.text: Cricketer of yore yearns to face spinner

indicators.note: to face means to stand in front of, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: to yearn is to long
a spinning top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: An old cricketer longs to bat against a spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a slow bowler but is the toy. A long stop is an old cricket fielding position straight behind the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder placed far behind the wicketkeeper, a position rarely used in modern cricket.

clue.text: A border we'd get trimmed at either end

indicators.note: cutting each end off the phrase leaves the letters within it

explanation.surface: A garden border that needs clipping at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed at either end' drops the W and T of 'we'd get'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rim or margin forming the outer boundary of something.

clue.text: Mother is composing a line to the weatherman

indicators.note: composing means arranging, so the letters of 'Mother is' are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A mother writes a note to the TV weather forecaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composing' rearranges MOTHERIS.
explanation.definitionFit: On weather maps, a line joining places of equal temperature is drawn for forecasters.

clue.text: They have no saving graces

parts.note: 'saving graces' read literally: people with no habit of saving money

explanation.surface: People with no redeeming qualities at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A saving grace is a redeeming feature; here it means thrift.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasteful people who squander money never put anything aside.

clue.text: Very little time for credit

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'just a second'

explanation.surface: Little time left for a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief instant, and informal British slang for buying on account.

clue.text: It may be said to be highly complimentary

definitions.text: It may be said to be highly complimentary

parts.words: It may be said to be highly complimentary
parts.note: a speech said aloud praising someone, often at a funeral

explanation.surface: Something one might describe as very flattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' is literal: this praise is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech of praise, typically for someone who has died, is full of compliments.

clue.text: Married Daisy, a teacher

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Daisy got married to a schoolteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' looks like a woman's name but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is a male teacher, so the word is a synonym.

clue.text: In retreat the general offers to withdraw

indicators.note: retreat means going backwards, so the hidden letters are read in reverse
In says the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the word break

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A defeated general pulls back and proposes to leave the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'In retreat' as one reversal signal; 'In' marks the hidden word, so EGENER sits across 'thE GENEral' and 'retreat' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back on a promise or offer is a way to withdraw from a commitment.

clue.text: M Poirot has a point –- a strong one

parts.note: Agatha Christie's Belgian detective is Hercule Poirot, M being Monsieur
a point of the compass, here S for south

explanation.surface: The famous detective has made a strong point in his deduction.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical hero of Greek legend is the byword for great physical strength.

clue.text: Dedication to a concern is unusual

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Commitment to a business is a rare thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges TOACONCERNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something holy, as a church is blessed and set apart for worship.

clue.text: Food preparation that's part of the service

definitions.meaning: a prepared item of food served at a meal
one plate or bowl from a dinner service set

explanation.surface: Something cooked in the kitchen that is part of what waiters do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is the set of matching tableware, not waiting at table.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe served at a meal and a piece of crockery from a matching set.

clue.text: Test site –- no place for ladies

definitions.text: Test site –- no place for ladies

parts.words: Test site –- no place for ladies
parts.note: ..., the London cricket ground that hosts Test matches, read as the plural of a nobleman's title, men rather than ladies

explanation.surface: A testing ground where women are unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground where Test (international) matches are played; its members' pavilion long barred women.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket ground's name doubles as noblemen, the male counterpart of ladies.

clue.text: A complaint I'd not put in a guide

indicators.note: not put in says the letters of I'd are left out of 'a guide'

parts.note: taken as the letters I and D

explanation.surface: Someone says they would leave a grievance out of a travel handbook.
explanation.walkthrough: AGUIDE loses ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A malarial fever with shivering fits is an old-fashioned illness, a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: Fuss, making rounds between hospitals over area

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first part sits above the next
between means placed inside, with an H either side

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, twice for the plural
O is a round shape, twice for the plural

explanation.surface: A doctor making a fuss on ward rounds between hospitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' are not ward rounds but circles, O's.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion or fuss over something trivial, informal slang.

clue.text: Father to confess and make headlines

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: A priest confessing a scandal that hits the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headlines' are lines on the forehead, not newspaper headings.
explanation.definitionFit: Scowling creases the brow, putting wrinkle lines on one's head.

clue.text: Challenge whether goose is cooked

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been worked over, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A query over whether the goose is done yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cooked' rearranges WHETHERGOOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry's traditional demand to an approaching stranger is a challenge.

clue.text: Tyrant will appear day Riot Act is reformed

indicators.note: reformed means made over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tyrant will rise the day the Riot Act is rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is reformed' rearranges RIOTACT.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler wielding unchecked power is a tyrant.

clue.text: Fast repeated punches

indicators.note: repeated means the word appears twice

parts.note: a chop is a short blow, a punch

explanation.surface: A boxer throws quick punches in succession.
explanation.definitionFit: An urging to hurry, meaning quickly or without delay.

clue.text: A question of double identity?

parts.note: asked when two things look alike and one cannot tell them apart

explanation.surface: A query about someone leading two lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a spy's double life but confusion between two similar things.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is asked when one cannot distinguish between two alike items, a question about identity.

clue.text: The academic field

parts.note: field read literally as the grounds of a university

explanation.walkthrough: An academic field is a subject; here it is the land a college stands on.
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds and buildings of a university or college form its site.

clue.text: Two articles supporting embargo for fruit

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means sitting below the other piece

parts.note: an embargo is a ban
an is an indefinite article
a is another indefinite article

explanation.surface: Grammar words propping up a trade ban on fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow tropical fruit is one example of fruit.

clue.text: It could contain jam but is certainly not jammed

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a pot that might hold preserves
slightly open, as a door that is not stuck shut

explanation.surface: A pot that might hold preserves is plainly not stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A JAR for the container; whole, it means a door left open.
explanation.definitionFit: A container for preserves, and a door standing slightly open, not wedged.

clue.text: It's an African language, but oddly includes English article

indicators.note: includes means one piece goes inside another
oddly means strangely, so the letters of 'but' are rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article in English

explanation.surface: A remark that an African tongue curiously contains an English word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English article' is the indefinite article, not something from England; 'oddly' scrambles 'but' into BTU around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of languages spoken across central and southern Africa, Swahili and Zulu among them.

clue.text: Stage favourite's making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a favourite is a pet, with the 's giving S

explanation.surface: A popular stage actor returns to the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' looks theatrical but means a phase; 'making a comeback' turns PETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A phase in a process, one stage of progress.

clue.text: Some distance away from a service, heading north

indicators.note: heading north in a down clue means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Away from a military service, travelling north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' turns RAF to FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary word for at a distance, from a long way off.

clue.text: Able to go where one likes for nothing

definitions.text: Able to go where one likes

explanation.surface: Someone at liberty to travel anywhere at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: At liberty to move unrestricted, and costing nothing.

clue.text: Don't cheat in two forms of leisure activity

parts.note: games or recreation, a form of leisure
a funfair, another kind of leisure activity

explanation.surface: Advice to be honest while enjoying two kinds of pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: To act honestly and by the rules is the opposite of cheating.

clue.text: Staff to support one who's disabled

definitions.text: Staff to support one who's disabled

parts.words: Staff to support one who's disabled
parts.note: staff read as a stick, not employees, used as a walking aid

explanation.surface: Employees hired to look after a disabled person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' is a stick, not a team of carers.
explanation.definitionFit: A walking aid that props up someone with an injured leg is a supporting stick.

clue.text: It could be faster on the promenade

indicators.note: could be means the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone might walk or run more quickly along the promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges FASTERON.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade is the paved walkway along the shore of a seaside town.

clue.text: Allow to rest peacefully? Quite the opposite

definitions.text: Allow to rest peacefully? Quite the opposite

parts.words: Allow to rest peacefully? Quite the opposite
parts.note: RIP (rest in peace) after 'let' seems to grant calm, yet the idiom means to act without restraint

explanation.surface: A wish for someone to be left in peace, then reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP is the gravestone abbreviation for rest in peace; the phrase actually means letting go wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to act with full force and no restraint, the opposite of resting.
